transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-20
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood CSM), Evelyn Cho (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (KiteCommerce Head of MLOps), Ben Turner (KiteCommerce CTO), Ravi Patel (KiteCommerce SRE), Maya Lopez (KiteCommerce Product)

Summary:
Quick QBR / health check focused on usage, cost trends, reliability incidents last quarter, and roadmap alignment for performance improvements and privacy requirements. Agreed to run dedicated benchmark and share compliance docs.

Topics:
- Usage and cost trends (embeddings pipeline, chat routes)
- Reliability & incidents (p99/p95 tail latency, error spikes)
- Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs and reserved capacity
- Roadmap: quantization, batching suggestions, and rollout plan
- Compliance: SOC2, VPC, KMS integration

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — this is Lena from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account, with Marco and Evelyn from our team. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Aisha: Doing well, thanks. Busy week. We wanted to focus on cost and the latency regressions we've seen.
[00:20] Marco: Great, we'll start with usage patterns, then go reliability, then next steps — sound good?
[00:26] Ben: Yeah that works. From our side, the embedding pipeline has ramped — about 3x in last quarter — and costs spiked. We're seeing higher token fees than expected.
[00:38] Evelyn: When you say token fees, is that mostly embedding calls or generation?
[00:42] Ben: Mostly embeddings. We moved some heavy batched ingest for search vector updates.
[00:47] Lena: Ok, good context. We've got a few levers here — batching, KV cache, and quantized model config — and a Dedicated capacity option if you need predictable throughput.
[00:58] Aisha: We're evaluating Dedicated but main concern is cost vs host. Also compliance — we need a VPC option and stronger KMS integration.
[01:07] Marco: We can definitely support VPC Private deployment; we've got an on-prem pattern too. I'll share SOC2 artifacts and our network diagram after the call.
[01:16] Ravi: One thing — our SREs noticed p99 spikes during daily re-index runs, around 02:00 UTC. Could be due to batch bursts.
[01:26] Evelyn: That aligns with prefix cache invalidation and long KV cache fill. Do you have logs for those times?
[01:30] Ravi: Yes, I'll drop them in the share.
[01:34] Ben: Also curious about quantization benefits — you mentioned q4_0 and int8 variants? Any tradeoffs on quality?
[01:42] Evelyn: Yeah, q4 and int8 can give 2-3x throughput gains and lower memory, but output sometimes changes a bit. We recommend running a small eval set — we'll help set that up.
[01:53] Lena: For cost modeling, we usually build per-route cost units and show where batching / caching reduces tokens billed.
[02:00] Maya: For product, we'd like predictable latency for user-facing chat. 200ms at p95 is our goal. What can we do?
[02:08] Evelyn: To hit 200ms p95 you'll likely want either a lower-latency model and reserved Dedicated slots, or aggressive caching for repeated prompts. Also optimize prompt length.
[02:18] Ben: If we go Dedicated, what's the commitment and SLA?
[02:22] Lena: Dedicated is reserved GPU pools — monthly or annual commit. We can share options; SLA covers uptime and latency targets with a support path.
[02:29] Aisha: Any quick wins we can implement before committing?
[02:32] Evelyn: Yes — enable prefix caching, tune batching window, and apply model quantization on non-critical routes. We can provide config templates.
[02:40] Ravi: On the reliability side, we saw intermittent 503s last month during a cloud provider maintenance window — were those from fallback routing?
[02:48] Marco: Possibly. Redwood does smart routing and fallback; sometimes service-to-service naming gets messy in logs and our auto-fallback increases latency. We'll correlate with your timestamps.
[02:58] Ben: We're also looking at cost allocation — can you provide token-level breakouts by route?
[03:02] Lena: Yes, our Console gives token-level cost and per-route dashboards. I'll include screenshots and an export.
[03:09] Aisha: About security — we need keys in HSM and audit logs for model access. Is that supported?
[03:16] Marco: We support KMS/HSM integrations and audit logging for Private deployments; details in the SOC2 package.
[03:22] Maya: Roadmap question: any upcoming improvements that could help our latency/cost?
[03:26] Evelyn: We're rolling out improved kernel selection and better batching heuristics next quarter, plus more quantized model variants. Could reduce both latency and cost.
[03:35] Ben: Nice. For the benchmark, what inputs do you need from us?
[03:38] Evelyn: Sample prompts, typical token lengths, concurrency targets — and one week of tail latency logs. We'll also run dedicated vs hosted comparisons.
[03:45] Ravi: We'll prepare those. We might also want a quick load test during low-traffic windows.
[03:50] Lena: Sounds good.
[03:52] 
[04:00] -- mid-call check --
[04:05] Aisha: A few questions from procurement — about contract term flexibility and early termination for Dedicated.
[04:12] Lena: We can be flexible on term and have phased pilots before annual commits; procurement and I will sync.
[04:18] Ben: Any benchmarking data comparing Redwood to Anthropic/OpenAI for our use-case?
[04:23] Evelyn: We have internal perf numbers and a model catalog with verified profiles; we'll share a concise bench sheet but recommend running your own too.
[04:30] Maya: Can you also advise on embedding dimensionality — we're using 1024 dims right now — any cost/quality tradeoffs?
[04:37] Evelyn: Lower dims reduce storage and cost but might reduce retrieval quality; we can simulate recall metrics on a sample.
[04:43] Ravi: On logging retention — our policy requires 90 days. Redwood default is 30; can that be extended?
[04:50] Marco: Yes, retention add-ons are available. We'll include pricing.
[04:54] Aisha: Great. On the action side, let's prioritize cost breakdown and a benchmark.
[04:59] Lena: Agreed — action items noted. We'll reconvene after initial bench.
[05:06] Ben: One small thing — in the Console some route names appear truncated so our dashboards mismatch. Can that be fixed?
[05:12] Marco: That's a UI bug; we'll log it and track it.
[05:16] Maya: Ok, thanks everyone.
[05:20] Lena: Recap — Marco sends SOC2 and network diagram by Friday; Lena sends cost model and QBR deck by Monday; Evelyn schedules benchmark with Ravi for next week. Any other items?
[05:31] Aisha: No, that's it. Thank you.
[05:34] Lena: Thanks all.

End of transcript.

Notes: Some transcription uncertainty around product names (Redwood Dedicated sometimes heard as "Redwood Dedicate") and a few acronyms (KV cache transcribed as K V cache). References to shared artifacts: SOC2 packet link (sent post-call), QBR deck (to be shared), benchmark spreadsheet template (to be shared).
